description: We are Gravity Defiers, a passionate team of innovators, developers, and problem-solvers participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.
summary: The Unseen Legacy is an interactive virtual space museum built by Team Gravity Defiers that tells the story of humanity's space exploration through the machines we sent into the cosmos. Guided by the message "They were sent to explore. Some never returned. None were forgotten," visitors journey across four interactive chapters: from Apollo's lunar mass trade-offs and the silent scientific artifacts left on the Moon, to Voyager 1's active extended mission in interstellar space, and finally to the next generation of exploration comparing the Apollo Lunar Rover with NASA's Artemis Lunar Terrain Vehicle (LTV) and Voyager 1 with the Johns Hopkins APL Interstellar Probe concept.
details: What It Does & How It Works: "The Unseen Legacy" is an interactive, web-based virtual museum created by Team Gravity Defiers. Guided by our core message—"They were sent to explore. Some never returned. None were forgotten."—the platform takes visitors on a 4-chapter narrative journey across two extremes of space exploration: • Chapter 1 (Apollo & The Moon): Features an interactive Lunar Ascent Mass Budget Simulator demonstrating the rocket-equation physics behind why Apollo astronauts had to leave heavy equipment behind (2,730 kg liftoff limit vs. 2,150 kg descent stage) to safely return 382 kg of lunar samples. • Chapter 2 (The Heroes We Don't See): Showcases 4 lunar artifacts with official NASA NSSDCA IDs—Apollo 11 Descent Stage (1969-059C), Apollo 15 LRV (1971-063C), Surveyor 3 (1967-035A), and ALSEP Laser Retroreflectors (1969-059C-04)—paired with a live Earth-to-Moon Laser Ranging Simulator (2.564s round-trip light time showing the Moon receding at 3.8 cm/year). • Chapter 3 (Voyager 1 — The Machine That Kept Going): Distinguishes abandoned lunar relics from Voyager 1 (1977-084A), an active spacecraft on an extended interstellar mission over 24.6 billion km away, featuring a NASA Deep Space Network (DSN) 22W signal simulator. • Chapter 4 (The Future): Compares historical pioneers with next-generation missions through an Apollo LRV vs. NASA Artemis Lunar Terrain Vehicle (LTV) matrix and a 50-year trajectory simulator comparing Voyager 1 (3.6 AU/yr) with the JHUAPL Interstellar Probe concept (7.6+ AU/yr). Benefits & Intended Impact: Instead of viewing discarded spacecraft as "space junk," our project reframes planetary hardware as priceless scientific heritage. It educates students, researchers, and the public on orbital physics, ongoing passive lunar experiments, and future exploration policy under the Artemis Accords. Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used: • Frontend & Simulation Engine: HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS, and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+) for zero-dependency physics and telemetry calculations. • Visuals & UI: Custom HTML5 Canvas star-map rendering and a Dual-Theme system (NASA Orbital Onyx Dark Mode & Celestial Gold Star-Map Light Mode). • Deployment & Version Control: GitHub and Netlify/Vercel for instant browser access across desktop and mobile devices. How Our Project Is Creative & Factors Considered: Rather than building a static encyclopedia, we combined emotional scrollytelling with hands-on physics simulators. Our team carefully considered scientific accuracy (verifying every artifact with official NSSDCA IDs), accessibility (high-contrast dual color palettes), and the critical distinction between dormant lunar relics and active deep-space probes like Voyager 1.

Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle (NSSDCA ID: 1971-063C) - Electric rover specifications  & Hadley Rille location
Apollo 11 Laser Ranging Retroreflector (NSSDCA ID:  1969-059C-04) - Active passive quartz mirror array on the Moon:
NASA International Laser Ranging Service (ILRS) - Lunar recession rate (+3.8 cm/ year) & 2.564s laser round-trip  telemetry
Surveyor 3 Lunar Lander (NSSDCA ID: 1967-035A) – Pre-Apollo robotic lander & Apollo 12 inspection record
Voyager 1 Spacecraft Master Record (NSSDCA ID: 1977-084A) - Trajectory, Grand Tour flybys  & Golden Record metadata
Voyager 1 Plasma Science Experiment (NSSDCA ID: 1977-084A-06) - Heliopause crossing telemetry (121.6 AU)
NASA Voyager Mission Status Portal - Real-time distance (>24.6B km) & RTG power  status
NASA Deep Space Network Now (DSN) - Live 22W X-Band carrier & 160 bps downlink  telemetry
Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (JHUAPL) Interstellar Probe Study (~7.6+ AU/yr, 50-year mission concept)
